title: Continuing education units and delivery formats as 247 CMR 2.00 defines them
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 2.00 a Contact Hour is a unit of measure of educational credit which is a minimum of 50 minutes, or the equivalent as determined by the Board, of satisfactory participation in a Board-approved program of continuing education, and a Continuing Education Unit is equal to ten contact hours or its equivalent as determined by the Board. Continuing Education means participation by registered pharmacists in Board-approved educational programs and is a prerequisite for the renewal of a personal registration. Home-study and Other Mediated Instruction means continuing education activities which do not provide for direct interaction between faculty and participants and may include audio tapes, video tapes, cable television, computer assisted instruction, journal articles and monographs. A Live Program is a continuing education program that provides for direct interaction between faculty and participants and may include lectures, symposia, live teleconferences and workshops. A Board-approved Program is one approved by the Board for continuing education credits; it may be sponsored by ACPE, or sponsored or co-sponsored by a person granted prior written approval by the Board for the particular program, and the Board may, within its discretion, accept comparable continuing education hours approved by other Boards of Pharmacy.
exam_relevance: Tests the unit behind every continuing education count and the direct-interaction test that decides whether an hour falls under the home-study ceiling.

common_confusions: A live teleconference is a live program: the test is direct interaction between faculty and participants, not physical presence.
A contact hour is a minimum of 50 minutes, not a 60-minute clock hour.
verification_notes: Read in the current official Board of Registration in Pharmacy publication of 247 CMR 2.00 on mass.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed. A fresh independent audit is still required before any section relying on it is published.
